A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PROPS research. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and Appendices A.1–A.7 support reliable comparison despite reformatting, relocation and table renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original alignment experiments, comparisons against RR and DP-SGD, intermediate-model error-estimator validation, and stage-count evaluations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds runtime measurements for GPT2-Medium and GPT2-Large in Appendix A.1, Table 5.

M1.justification: The staged RR privatization, disjoint data partitions, intermediate-model predictions, error-rate estimator, MLE labeling and DPO updates remain unchanged, as does the RLHF adaptation in A.5. Algorithm 1 clarifies the existing procedure without establishing a substantive method change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate binary preference alignment using truthy-dpo-v0.1, HH-RLHF and AlpacaEval. The added legal-domain motivation and possible extension to multiple preferences are not evaluated coverage; the runtime experiment introduces no identified new dataset or task.

E2.justification: RR and DP-SGD remain the alignment baselines, and the oracle, stage-count and qualitative comparison participants are retained. The new timing table compares PROPS with the existing RR comparator.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a 500-entry runtime evaluation separating DPO training and label-generation time for GPT2-Medium and GPT2-Large. Section 4 also removes v1's conflicting batch-size-4/two-epoch statement and retains one DP-SGD epoch, consistent with the existing appendix; this reporting correction does not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix A.1 adds an empirical overhead analysis identifying label generation as the dominant additional cost. Section 4 newly reports qualitatively that a clipping threshold of C=1 harmed utility. The existing stage-count analysis, estimator validation and response case studies are unchanged.

E5.justification: The appendix retains the same mean-and-standard-deviation reporting and five consecutive trials for the stage-count comparison. No new seed information, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty procedures are introduced, including for the timing results.

E6.justification: New Table 5 reports RR versus PROPS total times of 42 seconds versus 5 minutes 13 seconds for GPT2-Medium, and 1 minute 53 seconds versus 13 minutes 29 seconds for GPT2-Large, on 500 entries. Existing performance tables, oracle-error values and illustrated responses are unchanged. The C=1 clipping observation is also a new qualitative finding.

T1.justification: The privacy definitions, Lemma 1, Theorem 1, estimators and derivations in A.2–A.4 are mathematically unchanged. The new discussion of theoretical applicability qualifies interpretation without revising assumptions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the main privacy, method and headline performance claims. Section 1 newly identifies private intermediate-model error estimation as the core novelty and claims provably better labels than either noisy signal alone, strengthening the stated contribution.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly states the binary-preference scope and cautions that its idealized theory is not directly predictive for Transformers. Section 4 expands stage selection into a privacy-dependent interpretation involving noise propagation and data availability, while A.1 adds a computational-cost versus utility discussion.

D1.justification: Appendix A.1 newly discloses training and label-generation times and the 500-entry measurement scale. Existing data-processing instructions, hyperparameter table, evaluation prompt and code/data links are retained. Hardware for the new timings is not specified.

R1.justification: v2 adds Zhu et al. (2023) on pairwise or k-wise comparisons and explicitly positions PROPS relative to self-training through its private error-estimation mechanism. The remaining related-work coverage and comparisons with Label-DP, multi-stage RR and PATE are retained.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites expand the motivation, distinguish privacy noise from model error, and explain stage selection. Algorithm wording is cleaned up and acknowledgments are added, while the main section order and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: The paper-wide conversion to TMLR formatting substantially changes the title/author block, typography, text width, running headers and placement of figures and tables. Algorithm 1 gains numbered steps and a runtime table is added. Existing figure content is retained.

improvement.justification: The runtime measurements, clearer DP-SGD epoch description and explicit theoretical limitations improve transparency. However, Section 1 newly claims provably better labels than either signal alone, whereas the unchanged A.4 derivation says the MLE matches the lower-error signal. These useful clarifications coexist with a substantive overstatement of the central mechanism, preventing a reliable judgment of net overall improvement.
